\chapter{Clear or vague}
\label{ch:ar-clear-or-vague}
\hlchaptermodality{417}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say vague, frank and specific, and say that something became evident or that someone referred to it.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 417: I can say vague, frank and specific, and say that something became evident or that someone referred to it.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{غامض} (ghāmiḍ)}{غامض (ghāmiḍ)}]{\ar{غامض} (ghāmiḍ) — vague}

\label{lesson:AR-C417-ghamid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for insurance, then the Arabic for apart from.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{غامض}}
\textbf{\ar{غامض}} — \emph{ghāmiḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}vague\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{جوابه} \ar{غامضا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna jawābuhu ghāmiḍan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His answer was vague.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{غامض}} (\emph{ghāmiḍ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-m-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be hidden, unapparent\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ghāmiḍ} is the active participle: what is hidden, obscure, vague.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāmiḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāmiḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna jawābuhu ghāmiḍan.} — His answer was vague.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for insurance, then the Arabic for apart from, then say \emph{ghāmiḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{غامض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Vague\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صريح} (ṣarīḥ)}{صريح (ṣarīḥ)}]{\ar{صريح} (ṣarīḥ) — frank}

\label{lesson:AR-C417-sarih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for apart from, then the Arabic for vague.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صريح}}
\textbf{\ar{صريح}} — \emph{ṣarīḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}frank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{صديقي} \ar{صريحا} \ar{معي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna ṣadīqī ṣarīḥan maʿī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My friend was frank with me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صريح}} (\emph{ṣarīḥ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-r-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}pure, unmixed, clear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ṣarīḥ} is what is pure and unmixed: plain, frank.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣarīḥ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for apart from, then the Arabic for vague, then say \emph{ṣarīḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محدد} (muḥaddad)}{محدد (muḥaddad)}]{\ar{محدد} (muḥaddad) — specific}

\label{lesson:AR-C417-muhaddad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for vague, then the Arabic for frank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محدد}}
\textbf{\ar{محدد}} — \emph{muḥaddad} — \textquotedblleft{}specific\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وصل} \ar{الضيوف} \ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{المحدد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waṣala aḍ-ḍuyūf fī al-waqt al-muḥaddad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The guests arrived at the set time.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محدد}} (\emph{muḥaddad}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to sharpen; to set a limit\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Muḥaddad} is the Form II passive participle of \emph{ḥaddada}, to specify: fixed, specific.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥaddad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waṣala aḍ-ḍuyūf fī al-waqt al-muḥaddad.} — The guests arrived at the set time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for vague, then the Arabic for frank, then say \emph{muḥaddad} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اتضح} (ittaḍaḥa)}{اتضح (ittaḍaḥa)}]{\ar{اتضح} (ittaḍaḥa) — to become evident}

\label{lesson:AR-C417-ittadaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for frank, then the Arabic for specific.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اتضح}}
\textbf{\ar{اتضح}} — \emph{ittaḍaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to become evident\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اتضح} \ar{أن} \ar{الطريق} \ar{مغلق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ittaḍaḥa anna aṭ-ṭarīq mughlaq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It became evident that the road was closed.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتضح}, \emph{yattaḍiḥ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اتضح}} (\emph{ittaḍaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ḍ-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be clear, plain\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to make itself plain: to become evident. \ar{واضح}, clear, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittaḍaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittaḍaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittaḍaḥa anna aṭ-ṭarīq mughlaq.} — It became evident that the road was closed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for frank, then the Arabic for specific, then say \emph{ittaḍaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اتضح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To become evident\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أشار} (ashāra)}{أشار (ashāra)}]{\ar{أشار} (ashāra) — to refer}

\label{lesson:AR-C417-ashara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for specific, then the Arabic for to become evident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أشار}}
\textbf{\ar{أشار}} — \emph{ashāra} — \textquotedblleft{}to refer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أشار} \ar{المعلم} \ar{إلى} \ar{خطأ} \ar{في} \ar{الجملة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ashāra al-muʿallim ilā khaṭaʾ fī al-jumla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher drew attention to a mistake in the sentence.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشير}, \emph{yushīr}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{أشار} \ar{إلى} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أشار}} (\emph{ashāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to take honey; to give a sign\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, to make a sign to someone: to refer, to indicate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashāra al-muʿallim ilā khaṭaʾ fī al-jumla.} — The teacher drew attention to a mistake in the sentence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for specific, then the Arabic for to become evident, then say \emph{ashāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أشار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To refer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
